title: MessageIds form leaks invalid bytes into result vec
description: Trigger: parse_header_typed(HeaderForm::MessageIds, b"not-an-id") or any input where mail-parser's parse_id() finds no <...> tokens but accumulates token_invalid_start>0. parse_id returns HeaderValue::Text(<lossy UTF-8 of invalid range>). text_list() in header_typed.rs:352-358 maps HeaderValue::Text(s) to vec![s.to_owned()] without distinguishing it from a single valid stripped msg-id. The module doc (lines 20-22) and RFC 8621 §4.1.2.5 require malformed input to yield an empty Vec. Currently malformed input yields a one-element vec containing the unparsed garbage. Probe: cargo test -- with assert_eq!(parse_header_typed(HeaderForm::MessageIds, b" not an id"), HeaderValueTyped::MessageIds(vec![])) — expected to fail today. Fix: in HeaderForm::MessageIds arm, only accept HeaderValue::TextList; OR reject single-element HeaderValue::Text results unless they look like a valid msg-id (no whitespace, no angle brackets). The cleanest fix is to inspect mail-parser's id.rs invariants and only forward results that came through the <>-stripping branch.
close_reason: Fixed: MessageIds form now distinguishes mail-parser's valid single-Text result (bracket-stripping branch) from broken-client recovery (no brackets in input). Added regression test for inputs with no angle brackets and inputs with @-but-no-brackets. Both must yield empty vec per RFC 8621 §4.1.2.5.
